entities.summary: Rudolph John Chauncey Fisher was an American physician, radiologist, novelist, short story writer, dramatist, musician, and orator. His father was John Wesley Fisher, a clergyman, his mother was Glendora Williamson Fisher, and he had two siblings. Fisher married Jane Ryder, a school teacher from Washington, D.C. in 1925, and they had one son, Hugh, who was born in 1926 and was also nicknamed "The New Negro" as a tribute to the Harlem renaissance. Fisher had a successful career as an innovative doctor and author, who discussed the dynamics and relationships of Black and White people living in Harlem.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent figure in the Harlem Renaissance, Rudolph Fisher's work addressed the dynamics and relationships between Black and White people living in Harlem, contributing to a more nuanced understanding of racial tensions and social change. His writing also helped pave the way for future generations of African American authors.
